comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral findings (C25-C30). Both evaluations find the evidence robust and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor while peer reviewers describe the behavioral results as 'solid' and supporting the main hypothesis.

Complete agreement on trajectory alignment evidence (C31-C33). Both evaluations accept the correlation patterns as key evidence for the compression mechanism. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment while peer reviewers integrate this into their overall positive evaluation of behavioral evidence.

Full agreement on basic neural decoding capabilities (C34-C36). Both evaluations accept the IEM decoding results without critique. OpenEval notes consistency with behavioral performance; peer reviewers acknowledge the multivariate decoding as part of solid evidence base.

Significant disagreement on neural replay evidence (C37-C41 vs C38-C41, C42-C43, C72, C103). Peer reviewers are less convinced about ruling out alternative explanations.

Partial overlap on replay dynamics (C42-C43). OpenEval finds temporal dynamics supported despite moderate correlation strength. Peer reviewers group these claims with broader replay findings (R4) and express uncertainty about interpretation, noting compatibility with multiple mechanisms.

Disagreement on trajectory encoding/reactivation (C44-C47). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong neural evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the evidence 'occurs only briefly in the late encoding phase' and expressing concern about the strength of findings.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding brain-behavior relationships (C48-C49, C101). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes crude methodology. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN and specifically critique the link as 'fairly weak and based on a potentially circular analysis,' showing stronger skepticism.

Additional overlap on C48 between OpenEval R7 and peer R5. Both express concerns about the brain-behavior link, with peer reviewers specifically critiquing the circularity of the analysis while OpenEval notes the median-split approach is crude.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty regarding retention period findings (C50). Both evaluations note the results are less clear than other periods. OpenEval calls interpretation 'speculative'; peer reviewers characterize it as 'some evidence,' indicating weaker confidence.

Agreement on overall conclusions (C51, C61, C79 vs C51, C73, C79, C105). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multi-level convergence of evidence. Peer reviewers state 'the balance of evidence appears to favour the compression account' despite concerns about specific mechanisms.

Disagreement on ruling out confounds (C103-C105 vs C104). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing the dissociation as critical for establishing spontaneous replay. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting findings remain 'consistent both with compression-based and conventional rehearsal mechanisms.'
